name: Rating
propertyCopy: Icon size, label and selected count are properties of the same component, not separate icons - change them below to check this control's style and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Rating is a row of identical icon buttons (stars or hearts) that fill in as the user hovers or taps, letting someone score something on a simple, bounded scale - built for quick, low-friction feedback rather than precise numeric entry. When to Use A product or service review score - a 0-5 star rating. A quick satisfaction survey question - how satisfied were you, on a small fixed scale. A content quality score - used internally to flag good or poor examples. When Not to Use A precise numeric value - use Number - Rating is for a small, discrete, low-precision scale, not exact figures. A scale bigger than a handful of points - beyond roughly 5-10 points, individual icons stop being scannable at a glance; consider Slider or Number instead. A binary yes/no signal - use Switch or a simple Checkbox rather than a rating scale for a single up/down choice. Best Practices Preview the would-be selection on hover before it's committed by a click/tap, so users can see what they're about to choose. Keep the icon count small and fixed (commonly 5) - a rating scale should be scannable in a single glance. Pair the icon row with a numeric or text label when precision matters (e.g. "4.5 out of 5"), since icons alone can't show fractional values clearly. Do and Don't Do Rate this article A single five-point scale for one clear question - quick to answer and quick to read back in aggregate. Don't AccuracyToneDepthUsefulness Four scales turn a two-second reaction into a survey, and most people abandon it rather than score every dimension. Accessibility Each icon is an independently focusable, labeled control ("Rate 3 out of 5"), not one giant unlabeled row. The current and hovered/previewed value are both announced to assistive technology, not communicated by fill color alone. Fully operable by keyboard - arrow keys move between values, Enter/Space commits the selection.
